author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Courteney Cox returned to feature-film directing after a 12-year gap with “Evil Genius,” a true-crime thriller that premiered Saturday at the Toronto International Film Festival. The film revisits the 2003 “pizza bomber” case in Erie, Pennsylvania, in which delivery driver Brian Wells died after being forced to rob a bank with an explosive device locked around his neck.

Patricia Arquette plays Marjorie Diehl-Armstrong, who was convicted in connection with the plot, while David Harbour portrays her former fiancé and accomplice Bill Rothstein. The story centers on the pair’s destructive relationship and the chain of crimes surrounding the robbery. Cox said the production aimed for a tone that could hold the case’s bizarre details, dark humor and lethal consequences without turning it into a conventional procedural.

The project draws on a case previously examined in a 2018 Netflix documentary series, but shifts the focus toward a dramatized account of the people behind the scheme. For Cox, best known to many viewers for acting in “Friends” and the “Scream” franchise, the TIFF premiere marks a renewed move behind the camera and puts the film before distributors and festival audiences.
dek: “Evil Genius” dramatizes the 2003 Pennsylvania pizza-bomber case and stars Patricia Arquette and David Harbour.
headline: Courteney Cox returns to film directing with TIFF true-crime thriller
